rule: Automated reviewer identity is single-sourced in the reviewer-identity.jq module and every consumer routes through it
description: The automated-reviewer registry (which products are automated reviewers, their logins, and their approval-signal kind) and the identity predicates over it (`strip_bot`, `is_self`, `reviewer_matches_filter`, `reviewer_is_approver`) live in exactly one place: plugin/skills/github-review-loop/scripts/reviewer-identity.jq. Consumers reach it two ways: the jq filters fix-history-classify.jq and the three jq programs inside pr-change-detect-poll.sh carry `include "reviewer-identity";`, and every shell call site that runs fix-history-classify.jq passes the module search path with `jq -L <dir holding the module>` (prefilter.sh directly; fetch-normalize.sh through _shared/fetch-normalize-core.sh, which derives that dir from the classifier path). The identity predicates gate on the author's account type, so every GraphQL selection whose rows reach a type-gated predicate requests `author { login __typename }`. This fixture owns three axes. (1) CANONICAL CLAIM. The source pin sits on the registry declaration `def automated_reviewers:` in reviewer-identity.jq: deleting or renaming the registry turns the suite red. The registry entries themselves are deliberately unpinned so adding or editing a reviewer product does not break the suite; registry content is proved by the behaviour suites, not here. The self predicate is pinned on `def is_self($login; $type; $self): $type == "User"` in reviewer-identity.jq, a span that carries both the definition name and its account-type gate, so deleting or renaming `is_self` or dropping the `User` type gate (reverting self identity to a login-only compare) turns the suite red. (2) CONSUMER WIRING. pr-change-detect-poll.sh is pinned three times, once per jq program, on a span covering the `-L "$SCRIPT_DIR"` invocation AND the `include "reviewer-identity";` that opens the program body, so dropping either the search path or the include at any call site stops the match. The two slurping programs share the same invocation text, so their pins also carry the input each one reads (`"$reaction_rows" \ | jq -s` and `"$review_rows" \ | jq -s`): each pin can match only its own call site, and one surviving call site cannot keep the other's pin green. prefilter.sh is pinned on its classifier invocation `jq -r -L "$SCRIPT_DIR" -f "$CLASSIFY_FILTER"`. _shared/fetch-normalize-core.sh is pinned on its classifier invocation `jq -c -L "$classify_module_dir" -f "$classify_filter_path"` and on the derivation that binds that dir to the classifier's own directory, so pointing `-L` anywhere else fails. The query literals are pinned per selection on spans that include the neighbouring field list (`nodes { author { login __typename } body url reactionGroups` and so on), because the bare substring `author { login __typename }` also appears in header comments of fetch-normalize.sh and would survive the query losing `__typename`. The poll's comment and review-thread selections feed the type-keyed self predicate `is_self`, so they are pinned too, on spans that include the parent connection (`comments(last: 50) { totalCount nodes { databaseId author { login __typename } } }` and `comments(last: 1) { nodes { databaseId author { login __typename } } }`), because the bare node selection `nodes { databaseId author { login __typename } }` occurs in both and a bare pin would survive either one losing `__typename`. The poll judges a `review-approved` approval from GitHub's per-author latest reviews through an exhaustive paginated walk in a query of its own (gh follows one paginated connection per query), so its selection is pinned on the span `latestReviews(first: 100, after: $endCursor) { pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor } nodes { state author { login __typename } } }`, which carries the connection name, its page size, the cursor argument, the page-info selection gh follows to the next page, the review state, and the account type together: dropping the connection, its cursor argument, its `pageInfo`, its `state`, or its `__typename` stops the match. `first: 100` is the page size, not a bound on how many authors are read. That pin is the only static guard against the query losing the approval source, its pagination, or its account type. The pagination contract is also enforced behaviourally: the fake gh in tools/test_change_detect_poll.sh serves pages after the first only when the whitespace-normalized query declares `$endCursor: String`, passes `after: $endCursor`, and selects `pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor }`, and it serves a failed later page as a non-zero exit, so `approval:latest-reviews-every-page-read` goes red when the walk stops at page 1 and `approval:latest-reviews-partial-walk-fails-closed` goes red when a partial walk is judged instead of failing the capture. RESIDUALS for that pin: it proves the selection is present in the query text, never that the approval derivation uses it; it does not carry the `$endCursor: String` declaration or the `--paginate` flag, which only the behaviour cases cover; and those cases run against a fake gh that models gh's documented pagination contract, so a divergence between that model and real gh is invisible to this suite. These query pins are the ONLY guard on query drift: the behaviour tests inject payloads and bypass the live GraphQL queries entirely, so a query that stopped requesting `__typename` would make every type-gated predicate silently reject every author while the tests stay green. (3) INCLUDE IS LIVE CODE, AND NO SECOND COPY. set_check extracts, from lines whose first non-blank token is the literal (comment lines begin with `#` and never match), either `include "reviewer-identity";` or a definition of one of the module's six names (`def automated_reviewers`, `def approval_kinds`, `def strip_bot`, `def is_self`, `def reviewer_matches_filter`, `def reviewer_is_approver`). fix-history-classify.jq and pr-change-detect-poll.sh are checked in `equal` mode against the single-member set {include}: this proves the include sits on a real code line (fix-history-classify.jq also names the include inside a header comment, so a plain presence pin there would survive deleting the live include), and any redefinition of a module name in those files is an extra and fails. prefilter.sh, fetch-normalize.sh, and _shared/fetch-normalize-core.sh are checked in `subset` mode against the same set, so a module name redefined inside any of their embedded jq programs fails. The capture group is a fixed literal alternation rather than a negated-delimiter class because the axis is presence of one known literal plus absence of known definition literals, not membership of an enumerable marker set: a broad `def [a-z_]+` capture would also see each consumer's own legitimate helper definitions. RESIDUALS, stated plainly: these pins claim word-sequence presence in the named files, never meaning, and never that the code executes. A NEW consumer file not named here is invisible: a new script that queries review authors without `__typename`, invokes the classifier without `-L`, or re-declares the registry is not caught (set_check `files` is a literal list with no glob expansion). A rewrite that keeps every pinned substring while bypassing the module — for example matching inline login literals in a consumer that still includes the module — is not caught by this fixture; the closure test in tools/test_fix_history_classify.sh covers reintroduction of registry login literals. A second copy of the registry under a different name, or one whose `def` is wrapped so the name does not follow `def ` on the same line, is invisible to the set_check because extraction is line-scoped and case-sensitive. The `is_self` pin proves the definition's word sequence is present, not that any consumer calls it: a consumer that drops its `is_self` call in favour of a login-only compare keeps this fixture green. The self-compare closure check in tools/test_fix_history_classify.sh covers login-only self compares in the consumer files it names; a NEW consumer file is invisible to it as well.
